name: Hyperbolic

modes.label: H100 SXM · on-demand (marketplace floor)
modes.note: $3.19/GPU-h "starting at" price on hyperbolic.ai/marketplace (2026-09-28); "Pricing is refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers". Marketplace floor, not a firm quote; host CPU/RAM, region and billing increment unpublished. No charges for failed instances.

modes.label: H200 · on-demand (marketplace floor)
modes.note: $3.99/GPU-h "starting at" price on hyperbolic.ai/marketplace (2026-09-28); "Pricing is refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers". Marketplace floor, not a firm quote; host CPU/RAM, region and billing increment unpublished. No charges for failed instances.

modes.label: B200 · on-demand (marketplace floor)
modes.note: $5.99/GPU-h "starting at" price on hyperbolic.ai/marketplace (2026-09-28); "Pricing is refreshed weekly based on the best available rates from suppliers". Marketplace floor, not a firm quote; host CPU/RAM, region and billing increment unpublished. No charges for failed instances.

modes.label: Reserved term (prepaid, 7/14/30 days)
modes.commit_note: Paid up front in full; no early termination; discount vs the on-demand rate from the public reserve-options API: 7 d = 1%, 14 d = 3%, 30 d = 5% (app banner says 'Save up to 10% by making a reservation for rentals of one week or longer'). Reservation Protection (default on) rolls into on-demand billing at term end.
modes.note: Rate = locked on-demand GPU rate x (1 - discount). Not modelable exactly without the per-offer on-demand price.

modes.label: Private Cloud (single-tenant, >1 year contract)
modes.note: Custom contract, 'typically $1M+ deployments', billed outside credits; H100/H200/B200/B300.

plans.name: On-demand
plans.note: Hyperbolic's 'Pro' tier: prepaid credits only. 'You must deposit at least $5 one-time to automatically become a pro-tier user.' Credits 'never expire'. There's no monthly fee or commitment. At launch the balance must cover 1 hour of ALL running + new instances. When the balance hits zero, running instances 'may be terminated'. Storage volumes get a 30-day grace period, then are terminated. Auto Top-Up is optional and re-checks every 10 minutes.

caveats: Old hyperbolic.xyz/pricing returns 404. New official marketplace has weekly refreshed starting prices. No charges for failed instances. Reservations paid upfront; <1 year reserved and >1 year Private Cloud.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.
On-demand GPU rates are marketplace floor ("starting at") prices, refreshed weekly from supplier bids: actual availability and price at launch may be higher. Host CPU/RAM is bundled and unspecified.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.
Reservation Protection is ON by default: at the end of a reserved term the instance keeps running and bills at the current on-demand rate until terminated.
On-demand price is locked per instance at creation, but Hyperbolic reserves the right to contact long-running below-market instances about a price increase.
Onboard local NVMe is included free with every instance (size varies by configuration; up to 24 TB per 8-GPU H100/H200 node) and is erased on termination.

fleet.verification: Fund account credits through Billing; terms allow Stripe fraud/verification checks.
fleet.notes: GPU-rental onboarding and terms do not publish a universal fresh-account instance/GPU cap or quota-increase SLA. Marketplace availability is separate from account approval.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Onboard storage is erased when the instance is terminated. Always save important data to persistent storage or external services before terminating an instance.
snapshot_auto.note: No stop/pause state exists (API offers create, reboot, terminate only); nothing is checkpointed. Onboard storage survives only a platform reboot.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Since onboard storage is erased on termination, implement appropriate backup strategies
snapshot_on_demand.note: No snapshot/image feature anywhere in llms-full.txt or the public OpenAPI 3.1 spec (0 occurrences of 'snapshot'); docs recommend rsync to a persistent volume or aws s3 sync. False rather than null because the complete public API surface is enumerated and has no such endpoint.

harness_api.note: Plain GPU VM / bare-metal rental; public API covers rentals, storage volumes, SSH keys, balance. No agent/harness product.

ingress_rules.quote: Inbound ports on your instance's public IP are closed by default except SSH. When you launch an instance, add the ports you need in the port configuration field of the launch form.
ingress_rules.note: Port-level only (API field customPorts, max 20 ports, at creation). After launch, port changes go through support ('editing ports on a running instance is on the roadmap'). No IP-source allowlists or auth'd URLs documented; port 22 always open for platform SSH.

guest_firewall.note: Full VMs and bare-metal servers with sudo as ubuntu (docs use sudo mkfs/mount); iptables/nftables should work. Not documented.

secret_proxy.note: No secrets feature at all: raw VM/bare metal accessed by SSH key; any credential you need must be placed on the machine yourself.

volume_attach.quote: Every GPU instance comes with onboard storage included, plus the option to attach persistent storage volumes.
volume_attach.note: Network-attached block volumes, 100 GB-10 TB, up to 1,000 MB/s, hourly charge (rate varies by region, shown in console), select regions only; survive termination; attach/detach via console or API (POST /v2/on-demand/storage-volumes/attach).

volume_shared.note: Read-only when shared (attach API takes an array rentalIds). Read-write shared storage across a cluster is a custom request via support/sales ('shared storage across a cluster — email support@hyperbolic.ai').

isolation.quote: us-east-1 | US East | H100, H200 | 1x, 8x | VM | Ethernet
isolation.note: Region table labels instances 'VM' (a few regions are 'Bare metal'); security page says 'Each GPU instance runs in an isolated environment... No shared memory or storage between tenant instances', full root SSH access. Specific hypervisor (KVM/cloud-hypervisor) is never named, so generic 'dedicated-vm' rather than guessing the exact tech.

image_oci.quote: Ubuntu with NVIDIA drivers and Docker preinstalled — bring your own frameworks or containers
image_oci.note: Instances boot a fixed Hyperbolic-provided Ubuntu image; Docker runs inside it, but there is no documented way to boot the machine itself from your own OCI/Docker image.

nested_virt.quote: Full SSH root access to your instances
nested_virt.note: No mention of /dev/kvm or nested virtualization anywhere in the docs; instances are themselves VMs (or bare metal in a few regions) with no documented nested-virt support. Derived/not offered.

desktop.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (headless SSH GPU rental; no VNC/RDP/streamed desktop in any doc).

browser.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain GPU VM/bare-metal rental, no managed browser).

computer_use.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (no desktop, so no screenshot/click driving API).

anti_bot.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (GPU compute rental, not a browsing/scraping product).

captcha_solving.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Inbound ports on your instance's public IP are closed by default except SSH.
egress_ip_type.note: Each instance gets its own datacenter-hosted public IPv4; no residential/mobile IP product exists.

snapshot.quote: Onboard storage is erased when the instance is terminated. Always save important data to persistent storage or external services before terminating an instance.
snapshot.note: No snapshot/checkpoint feature in docs or the public OpenAPI surface (create/reboot/terminate only); onboard NVMe survives only a platform reboot, not termination.

fork.quote: Master the full lifecycle of GPU instance management on Hyperbolic - from creation to termination, including monitoring, scaling, and troubleshooting.
fork.note: No clone/fork-machine feature documented; instances are created fresh from the base Ubuntu image, not cloned from an existing instance.

fork_running.quote: Master the full lifecycle of GPU instance management on Hyperbolic - from creation to termination, including monitoring, scaling, and troubleshooting.
fork_running.note: No fork feature exists at all (see fork), so cloning a running machine is not offered.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Onboard storage is erased when the instance is terminated.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork feature exists, so memory-preserving forks are not offered.

wake_on_request.quote: On-demand instances are billed continuously for the lifetime of the instance until they are terminated.
wake_on_request.note: No sleep/wake mechanism documented; an instance runs until you terminate it or your balance runs out, with no request-triggered auto-wake.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Instances may be automatically terminated if your account balance is no longer positive.
auto_stop_idle.note: The only automatic stop condition documented is balance-based termination (or a ~3h provisioning timeout for instances that never become ready); there is no CPU/idle-usage auto-stop.

live_resize.quote: Master the full lifecycle of GPU instance management on Hyperbolic - from creation to termination, including monitoring, scaling, and troubleshooting.
live_resize.note: No resize-in-place feature; changing GPU/CPU/RAM configuration requires creating a new instance.

agent_harnesses.quote: Ubuntu with NVIDIA drivers and Docker preinstalled — bring your own frameworks or containers
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Base image ships Ubuntu + NVIDIA drivers + Docker; no coding-agent (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) templates are mentioned anywhere in the docs.

own_agent_api.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. This is a GPU compute marketplace; there is no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent product.

mcp_server.note: No MCP server mentioned anywhere in the docs index, the full docs text, or the public API reference; only a REST API is offered.

lang_python.quote:
# Check Python and pip
python3 --version
pip3 --version
lang_python.note: The base Ubuntu image ships python3/pip preinstalled and all quick-start examples run python/pip directly with no separate install step.

inbound_https.quote: Inbound ports on your instance's public IP are closed by default except SSH. When you launch an instance, add the ports you need in the port configuration field of the launch form.
inbound_https.note: Provider exposes raw TCP ports on the instance's own public IP; there is no managed HTTPS URL / TLS termination service for exposed ports (raw_tcp_inbound only).

egress_allowlist.quote: Use firewalls - Reach out to us about your options; configuration differs across regions
egress_allowlist.note: No provider-side outbound allow/deny list product for On-Demand; 'Custom Firewall Rules' / VPN / private networking are listed only under Private Cloud, a separate >1yr contract offering, not the modeled on-demand/reserved product.

egress_http_rules.quote: Use firewalls - Reach out to us about your options; configuration differs across regions
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress control documented anywhere; only guest-level iptables/nftables (root access) would be possible, not a provider-side feature.

static_egress_ip.quote: Inbound ports on your instance's public IP are closed by default except SSH.
static_egress_ip.note: Each instance has its own public IPv4 for the life of the instance, but there is no separate 'static/elastic IP' product that persists across instance recreation; not documented as a distinct feature.

windows.quote: Ubuntu with NVIDIA drivers and Docker preinstalled — bring your own frameworks or containers
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (Ubuntu-only Linux GPU instances).

macos.quote: Ubuntu with NVIDIA drivers and Docker preinstalled — bring your own frameworks or containers
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (x86 Linux GPU/bare-metal cloud, no Apple hardware).

arm64.quote: Hardware: H100 80GB, H200 141GB, B200 192GB, B300 288GB, RTX Pro 6000 96GB
arm64.note: All listed hosts are x86 NVIDIA GPU servers/VMs; no ARM CPU option is mentioned anywhere.

self_host.quote: Hyperbolic is a GPU marketplace / on-demand GPU cloud.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Hyperbolic is a hosted marketplace of supplier GPU capacity, not distributable self-hostable software.

byoc.quote: Need dedicated, single-tenant infrastructure custom-built for your team? That's Private Cloud.
byoc.note: Private Cloud is Hyperbolic-hosted single-tenant capacity via a custom contract, not a deployment into the customer's own cloud account (no BYOC option documented).

open_source.quote: Hyperbolic On-Demand GPUs provide high-performance GPU capacity for training, fine-tuning, inference, benchmarking, and custom deployments.
open_source.note: Proprietary hosted marketplace platform; no OSI-licensed core product is published.

sso.quote: Sign in with Google or GitHub - We support single sign-on with Google and GitHub.
sso.note: Only consumer-style OAuth login via Google/GitHub is offered; no enterprise SAML/OIDC SSO for organizations is documented.

eu_data_residency.quote: For customers processing data subject to GDPR, Hyperbolic provides: ... Data residency options for EU-based processing
eu_data_residency.note: Corroborated by EU regions in the on-demand region table (eu-north-4/5/7/8, eu-west-1/3/4, uk-southeast-3).

max_session_h.quote: On-demand instances are billed continuously for the lifetime of the instance until they are terminated.
max_session_h.note: On-demand instances have no maximum runtime; they run until the user terminates them or the account balance is exhausted. Reserved terms are fixed by contract (7-30 days) rather than an hourly session cap.
